about.tagline: Local-first personal AI assistant · instant chat, background execution, memory & tools
about.envCheckHint: Expand only when troubleshooting startup or local dependency issues.

settings.aboutDesc: A local-first agent workspace. The daemon owns the data; this shell only renders it.

notifications.description: Receive native OS notifications when OPC needs your approval or finishes background work without pulling focus unnecessarily.
notifications.testSent: Test notification dispatched. If nothing appeared, check your OS notification permissions or Focus/Do Not Disturb status.
notifications.unsupportedNote: System desktop notifications are unavailable in the current environment.
notifications.generalDescription: Master switch and focus rules for when notifications should appear.
notifications.enableHint: Turn off to mute all native toast banners and taskbar/Dock alerts.
notifications.whenHint: In Background mode, focused chat stays silent, while blocking approvals, questions, and errors still notify if you are viewing Settings or Schedules.
notifications.eventsDescription: Choose which background events trigger desktop notifications.
notifications.eventNeedsActionHint: Notify immediately when a Worker pauses for shell, browser, desktop approval or asks for your input.
notifications.eventRepliesHint: Notify when the assistant finishes replying, delivers background results, or completes a schedule (coalesced to prevent spam).
notifications.eventErrorsHint: Notify when a root task fails or Watchdog escalates a stalled thread. Clicking jumps straight to the Execution Observatory.
notifications.deliveryDescription: Control notification audio, message preview visibility, and window attention cues.
notifications.soundHint: Turn off to send silent OS notifications without sound.
notifications.previewHint: Hide message snippets behind generic text when sharing your screen or presenting.
notifications.attentionHintWin: Flash the Windows taskbar button when background notifications arrive and clear automatically on focus.
notifications.attentionHintMac: Show unread badge counts on the Dock icon and bounce gently for blocking approvals or errors.
notifications.attentionHintGeneric: Update the app badge counter on background alerts and reset on window focus.

assistantTools.description: Configure time, weather, web research and calculation tools for Router and Workers.
assistantTools.localDescription: Requests are sent by the main process through the active network proxy.
assistantTools.timezoneHint: Leave blank to follow the system, or enter an IANA zone such as Asia/Shanghai or America/Los_Angeles.
assistantTools.cityHint: Weather uses this city by default. A request can name another city; device location is never read.
assistantTools.searchDescription: Configure search providers and use the switches to control which sources the assistant can call.
assistantTools.failoverHint: On failure, only configured and enabled sources are tried in Exa, Tavily, Firecrawl order.
assistantTools.noEnabledProvider: Configure and enable a source first
assistantTools.keyRequired: Configure an API key before enabling
assistantTools.toolsNote: First tools: current time, weather, web search, page extraction, site crawl and status, arithmetic and common unit conversion. Open-Meteo is used for non-commercial purposes.

browser.title: Personal Agent browser
browser.description: The browser is a native OPC capability, not exposed through MCP. It runs in the background by default, and every external side effect is gated by an approval card in the conversation.
browser.subtitle: Controllable, approvable and persistent browser execution for your Personal Agent.
browser.confirmStop: Disable the browser runtime? Your login profile will be kept.
browser.confirmRemove: Remove the agent-browser runtime and Chrome for Testing cache? Your login profile will be kept; Playwright caches shared with other apps may also be affected.
browser.confirmReset: Clear browser login state and site data? This cannot be undone.

status.uninstalledDetail: Install to let Workers use browser tools
status.enabledDetail: Browser access is open to Workers
status.installedDetail: Runtime ready; enable it when needed

browser.diskUsageHint: agent-browser runtime and Playwright browser cache
browser.downloadEstimateHint: Estimate only; actual download depends on platform and cache state
browser.enableHint: Workers can call native browser_* tools
browser.progressNote: The percentage is an estimate; actual time depends on the network and existing cache.
browser.domainDesc: One domain per line; *.example.com is supported. The block list takes precedence over the allow list.
browser.allowAllHint: Domains on the block list are still blocked.
browser.approvalDesc: High-risk actions pause the current Worker and wait for confirmation in the conversation.

approval.navigation: Opening a domain that is not allowed

browser.approvalHint: When off, this kind of action no longer raises an approval card automatically.
browser.approvalHintNavigation: Navigation outside the allow list always asks for approval first.
browser.footer: Sign-in, submit, download, upload, delete and publish actions show an approval card in this conversation; approving resumes the same Worker and task.

desktop.title: Desktop control
desktop.description: Expose the full agent-desktop CLI to Workers through native MCP. App selection and actions follow the runtime's supported capabilities.
desktop.subtitle: Let your Personal Agent observe and operate desktop apps through the native accessibility tree.

status.uninstalledDetail: Install before the Personal Agent can control desktop apps
status.enabledDetail: agent-desktop MCP is connected and its tools are available to Workers
status.installedDetail: Runtime ready; enable it when needed

desktop.noSurfaces: The runtime reported no available surfaces
desktop.enableHint: Workers can call the desktop tools provided by the runtime
desktop.permissionRequiredNotice: Desktop control is installed; grant the system accessibility permission
desktop.progressNote: Overall progress is estimated; download size is measured in real time.
desktop.inspectorDesc: Read the live accessibility snapshot of a running task. Only sessions OPC already created are read; no new desktop actions are started.
desktop.emptySnapshot: Once a task uses desktop control, its latest control tree and refs appear here.
desktop.footer: Runs in the background by default; open the inspector from task details to view the current window, accessibility snapshot and action trace.

llm.desc: Providers and models come from pi's built-in catalog; the default model and thinking level apply to the runtime.
llm.keyHint: Stored only in the main process, encrypted with the OS keychain; edits apply when you press Save.
llm.title: LLM models
llm.defaultDesc: The provider and model used by execution bodies. The assistant follows this by default when routing events, and can be given its own, lighter model on the Event routing page.
llm.thinkingHint: Only applies to models that support reasoning.
llm.defaultNotReady: Default provider "{{name}}" is {{status}}; the runtime cannot use that model.
llm.providersDesc: {{curated}} curated providers listed; pi ships {{total}} in total.
llm.catalogFootnote: See /model in pi for the full catalog.
llm.descAll: pi ships {{providers}} providers and ~{{models}} models; all of them are reachable here, with prices taken from pi's catalog and editable in place.
llm.providersDescAll: {{count}} providers, grouped as official / subscription / cloud / gateway / China / other.
llm.enableNeedsKey: Add an API key before enabling models
llm.defaultCleared: "{{name}}" was disabled, so the default model was cleared
llm.idHint: Unique id, written into config and the ledger.
llm.apiHint: pi supports {{count}} API kinds; all are selectable here.
llm.addProviderKeyHint: Optional — fill it in to use the provider right away, or add it later.
llm.fetchRequested: Fetch requested (had {{before}} models); success depends on the provider's /models endpoint and key
llm.apiKeyOnly: This provider logs in with an API key — no OAuth
llm.removeConfirm: Delete “{{name}}” with its models and key? This cannot be undone.

compaction.desc: When the context approaches the model limit, older turns are summarized. Thresholds are relative to the selected model's window.
compaction.modelHint: Thresholds are computed against this model's context window.
compaction.title: Context compaction
compaction.sectionDesc: Summarize older turns before the request would be cut off.
compaction.reserveHint: Start compacting when free context drops below this; recommended {{recommended}}.
compaction.backgroundHint: Start a background compaction this much earlier; 0 disables.
compaction.footnote: Passed straight to pi's compaction policy; applies to the next run.

image.desc: pi's image model type. The default image model will drive visual deliverables.
image.empty: No image models exposed by the current providers.
image.title: Image models
image.descProvider: Image models follow their provider: configure the credential, enable models and set prices here.
image.emptyProvider: No image models available yet — add one below, or check that the built-in catalog loaded.
image.configHint: Built-in models are enabled together with the provider config; save, then pick a default. The API key stays in the main process and is encrypted.
image.protocolHint: openai-images posts to /images/generations; openrouter-images uses OpenRouter chat completions (modalities=image); google-images uses Gemini generateContent.
image.unmatchedPricing: {{count}} models have no official price in pi's catalog; their values were kept.
image.enableNeedsKey: Add an API key before enabling models

video.title: Video models
video.descProvider: Includes 6 popular built-in video providers plus OpenAI-compatible gateways, with customizable Base URL, API Key, and custom models.
video.providersDesc: Built-in video generation providers and compatible gateways.
video.emptyProvider: No video models available yet — add one below.
video.enableNeedsKey: Add an API key before enabling models
video.klingKeyHint: Accepts a relay Bearer Token or official Kling AccessKey:SecretKey (JWT is signed automatically).

voice.title: Voice models
voice.desc: ASR turns recordings into text; TTS reads text aloud. Voice models reuse the provider's base URL and API key.
voice.asrDesc: Microphone → text, for chat input and meeting notes.
voice.ttsDesc: Text → speech, for reading agent replies and deliverables.
voice.emptyProvider: No speech models available yet — add one below, or check that the built-in catalog loaded.
voice.enableNeedsKey: Add an API key before enabling models
voice.configHint: Voice models are configured with their provider; the API key stays in the main process and is encrypted. Xiaomi's speech models reuse the xiaomi provider.
voice.billingHint: ASR is billed per audio hour (Xiaomi ¥0.5/hour); TTS is free for a limited time. Voice models are not token-priced, so no price columns are shown.

decision.title: Decision models
decision.desc: Jev (TypeSafe System One) does not generate text: it reads a state and answers typed yes/no, choice or score questions with probabilities and confidence. The protocol is POST /v1/systemone, not OpenAI's /chat/completions.
decision.providersDesc: Providers that expose classifier models — TypeSafe direct, the OpenRouter relay, or a custom gateway.
decision.emptyProvider: No decision models available yet — add one below, or check that the built-in catalog loaded.
decision.enableNeedsKey: Add an API key before enabling models
decision.keyPlaceholder: Paste a TypeSafe / OpenRouter API key
decision.configHint: Direct: https://api.typesafe.ai/v1 with model jev-latest. OpenRouter relay: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 with typesafe/jev-1.14. The API key stays in the main process and is encrypted.
decision.pricingHint: Jev bills input tokens only; output is free (~$0.042 per million tokens). There is no output text, so no output price column is shown.
decision.tryDesc: Runs the real decisions.classify path against the default model — answers come from the service, not a local mock.
decision.statePlaceholder: e.g. Our API integration started returning 500s about 20 minutes ago and order processing is down.
decision.instructionsPlaceholder: e.g. How urgent is this message?
decision.criteriaChoicesPlaceholder:
billing=Payment or subscription issues
technical=Bugs or integration problems
decision.criteriaLevels: Score levels (one per line, starting at 0)
decision.criteriaLevelsPlaceholder:
Can wait
Needs attention this week
Needs attention today
decision.needInstructions: Fill in the question instructions first
decision.needTwoChoices: At least two choices are required
decision.needTwoLevels: At least two score levels are required
decision.bridgeMissing: Not connected to the main process

selfcheck.desc: Live checks for native modules, sandbox, persistence and process isolation.

settings.appearanceDesc: The shell ships light-first; the dark theme is adapted in step.
settings.fontSizeHint: Scales the whole interface proportionally (like browser zoom).
settings.fontHint: Uses fonts already installed; no network fetch.

pricing.hint: USD per 1M tokens, cache priced separately. "Use pi prices" fills the full cost incl. context tiers.
pricing.applied: Matched {{matched}} models against pi's official pricing; {{unmatched}} had no match (left unknown, never invented)

auth.title: Sign-in & credentials
auth.hint: OAuth is implemented by pi's provider (PKCE / device codes); credentials are stored locally in credentials.json and resolved by pi per request.

facts.title: Workspace rules
facts.desc: Rules written here enter every executor's prompt; the same subject supersedes the old value (history kept).
facts.subject: Subject, e.g. delivery standard
facts.object: Value, e.g. always include a README

runs.title: Consolidation runs
runs.desc: Distills durable preferences, rules, and playbook lessons into local Markdown files. Missing model is recorded as skipped, not an error.
runs.autoRulesText: Every 8 new messages · 10m idle · 15s debounce on correction signals · before compaction

filters.noMatches: No consolidation runs match the active filters.

manualFeedback.empty: Checked recent context; no durable memory changes needed.

company.title: Personal preferences
company.description: Choose how the assistant communicates with you. Your name is optional; your avatar appears in the title bar.
company.name: Workspace name
company.nameHint: Shown in the title bar and on the card
company.userHint: Optional; the assistant will speak naturally without a name
company.brandDesc: Name, colours and visual identity — what the title bar and card show.
company.logoHint: PNG / JPG / WebP / GIF / SVG, square works best, up to 500 KB
company.userDesc: Your name is optional. Leave it blank and the assistant will speak naturally without using a name.
company.userAvatarHint: Shown in the title bar; a placeholder is used when empty
company.replyDesc: These preferences apply to every assistant reply. You can always ask for something different in chat.
company.replyInstructionsHint: For example: lead with the conclusion; include runnable examples for code. Up to 500 characters.
company.replyInstructionsPlaceholder: How would you like replies to be structured?
company.imageType: Use a PNG, JPG, WebP, GIF or SVG image
company.imageTooLarge: The image must be 500 KB or smaller
company.imageFailed: Could not read that image — try again
company.budgetHint: Workspace budget: crossing it hard-stops dispatch. The budget centre shows live usage.
company.assistantHint: Shown in chat welcome, assistant messages and input placeholder (defaults to Buddy).
company.goalPlaceholder: e.g. Hand the content work to my assistant

billing.desc: How money is decided and shown. The ledger is always USD; the rate only changes the CNY figure on screen.
billing.policyHint: Which number is charged for a call.
billing.displayHint: USD and CNY only. The rate is a manual planning value — no live quotes.
billing.currencyHint: Switching only changes the display; stored amounts are untouched.
billing.rateHint: CNY per 1 USD. Defaults to 7.3 and can be changed at any time.
billing.rateInvalid: The rate must be between 0.01 and 100 (up to 4 decimals)
billing.rateBlurHint: Leave the field or press Enter to apply.
billing.previewHint: Uses this month's real spend so you can confirm the rate before reading the reports.
billing.previewSampleHint: Every amount in the reports is converted at this rate
billing.footnote: The rate is display-only: the ledger stores USD, and historical charges keep the rate frozen at settlement time.

usage.desc: Inspect model calls, usage and pricing details. Unknown costs are never shown as zero.
usage.bridgeUnavailable: Usage service is unavailable. Restart the desktop app and try again.
usage.emptyBackfillPending: No trustworthy task totals were available to import; per-call tracking starts with new activity.
usage.coveragePending: Legacy task totals have not been imported
usage.coverageComplete: Legacy task totals imported (without per-call input/output breakdown)
usage.noPriceHint: Provider returned no billed cost and no unit rate was matched; configure rates under Models & Pricing.
usage.rateHint: Costs follow the existing pricing policy and currency settings.
usage.switchToTokens: No priced costs yet — switch to token view
usage.noChartData: No usage data in this range

network.description: Configure it once and model calls, image generation and workspace child processes all take this route. Saving applies immediately and survives restarts.
network.modeDesc: How every outgoing request finds its route. The default follows the system, so nothing about your current setup changes.
network.modeSystemHint: Use the operating system's proxy settings (macOS Network / Windows Internet Options).
network.modeDirectHint: Ignore every proxy, including the system one and any HTTP_PROXY in the environment.
network.modeManualHint: Send every request through the proxy server below.
network.systemNote: Following the system proxy. With no system proxy configured this behaves like a direct connection; you can switch back to manual at any time.
network.directNote: Direct connection: the app uses no proxy at all and ignores proxy environment variables.
network.serverDesc: HTTP, HTTPS (TLS to the proxy itself) and SOCKS5, with optional credentials.
network.protocolHint: HTTPS means the proxy port itself speaks TLS; local proxy apps usually use HTTP or SOCKS5.
network.addressHint: Hostname or IP, port 1–65535. Pasting a full URL strips the scheme for you
network.authHint: Leave empty when the proxy needs no login. The password is encrypted with the OS keychain and stored only on this machine.
network.bypassHint: Loopback (localhost / 127.0.0.1 / ::1) always stays direct. Separate entries with commas or spaces, e.g. *.corp.example.com
network.testDesc: Runs a real request with the current draft: dial the port, then reach the internet through the proxy and read the egress IP. Nothing is saved.
network.testHint: Proves the port is open and traffic actually takes the proxy
network.testNeedManual: Switch to manual mode to test
network.coverage: Covered: model and image requests in the main process, the renderer and embedded pages, and child processes such as git / npm started in the workspace.
network.unavailable: Proxy settings are unavailable in this environment

runtime.desc: Workspace-wide execution environments and permission boundaries: commands run via the selected Node and Python interpreters, while built-in OCR and shell rules apply locally.
runtime.globalNote: This is a workspace-wide setting: changes apply to the next tool call and never interrupt a running task.
runtime.nodeDesc: System Node wins by default; Electron's bundled Node is only the fallback when none is installed.
runtime.pythonDesc: Point at the system Python 3, or at the interpreter inside a venv / conda environment.
runtime.autoHint: Auto-select uses the first available interpreter
runtime.addDesc: Useful for an nvm version, a venv or a conda environment. Saving makes it active immediately.
runtime.addNodeDesc: Point to an nvm, fnm, or project-specific Node binary. Saving makes it the active Node runtime.
runtime.addPythonDesc: Point to a venv, uv, or conda interpreter. Saving makes it the active Python runtime.
runtime.kindHint: One Node and one Python can be active at the same time
runtime.binaryHint: Must be an executable; venv / conda variables and PATH are detected automatically
runtime.name: Environment name
runtime.nameHint: Leave blank to name it after its directory
runtime.ocrDesc: Lets the model read text inside pictures; the models and the recognition both run on this machine, so images never leave it.
runtime.ocrEnableHint: Ships with the app, nothing to install. When off, no employee is given the ocr_image tool.
runtime.ocrBroken: {{count}} file(s) of the bundled models are missing or damaged, so it cannot be turned on. Reinstall the app to restore them.
runtime.ocrDetailHint: Text joins every line in reading order, which is what you want for meaning. Lines keeps each line's position and confidence, which is what you want for tables and forms.
runtime.shellDesc: Controls how workers authorize terminal commands (bash, PowerShell, Python scripts) inside the task workspace.
runtime.shellWindowsNote: Windows has no OS-level container sandbox. File read/write tools remain confined to the task workspace, and uploaded attachments are copied into workspace inputs/ automatically.
runtime.shellModeHint: Ask per task shows an approval card before running commands; Auto runs workspace commands without prompts; Disabled blocks shell commands.

watchdog.desc: Runs in an isolated background process outside the main app: checks task stalls/loops, main-process heartbeats, and MCP connections, asking a model to evaluate off-track work when needed. It only performs safe external reconnects and never cancels running tasks.

incidentsSection.healthyDesc: The background guardian is checking task progress, heartbeats, and MCP health.

watchdog.askDesc: Read-only evidence query grounded in recorded incidents and actions, without modifying running tasks.
watchdog.askPlaceholder: e.g. Why did a task stall or loop recently?
watchdog.askNoAnswer: No answer was returned. Please try again.
quickQuestions: Why did a task stall or loop recently?
Are MCP connections and heartbeats healthy right now?
What needs my attention right now?
watchdog.actionsDesc: Audit log of safe whitelisted repairs (such as reconnecting dropped MCP servers); never terminates tasks.
watchdog.noActions: No automatic repairs have been triggered yet.
watchdog.policyDesc: Configure anomaly thresholds and judgement model; save threshold changes to apply.
watchdog.advancedDesc: Heartbeat timeout, escalation delays, and judgement/repair cooldowns; defaults work well for most setups.
watchdog.modelHint: Used only to evaluate whether a flagged task is off track; empty follows the default LLM.
watchdog.enabledHint: When off, incidents are still recorded silently without alerts or model calls.
watchdog.idleHint: Flags a task for stall inspection when no new tool call or step occurs within this window.
watchdog.repeatHint: Marks a task as looping after the same tool and arguments fail this many times.
watchdog.staleHint: No heartbeat signal within this window flags the main process as unreachable.
watchdog.recheckHint: Wait this long before rechecking a newly spotted anomaly to ignore brief blips.
watchdog.escalateHint: Unresolved issues lasting longer than this threshold are prioritized as needing input.
watchdog.judgeHint: Cooldown between semantic evaluations of the same incident to prevent repeated calls.
watchdog.actionCooldownHint: Cooldown before attempting another automatic reconnect for the same incident.

triage.desc: Incoming events pass two stages. The first applies fixed rules and makes no model calls; the second is an optional semantic pre-filter that may call a classification model. Both settings affect cost and latency only — neither drops events silently.
triage.fastDesc: Filters only events that are provably empty or carry no new information; everything else passes.
triage.sourcesHint: Unchecked sources are dropped silently; GitHub is unchecked by default.
triage.semanticDesc: Decides, for events that passed the rule filter, whether they are worth the assistant's attention.
triage.thresholdHint: A lower threshold costs less but misfires more; the three options are 0.5 / 0.7 / 0.9.
triage.footnote: Both stages fail open; these settings change cost, not whether an event is handled.
triage.routerModelNoChoices: No chat model is available yet: add a key and enable one under Settings → Models → LLM.
triage.classifierNoChoices: No classifier is enabled yet: enable one under Settings → Models → Decision, or this step will be skipped.
triage.channelsLinkTitle: External app connections moved to Channels
triage.channelsLinkDesc: Feishu, DingTalk, and external messaging apps now connect bidirectionally via long-lived connections without local ports or tunnels.
triage.channelsLinkHint: Manage bot credentials, DM pairing approvals, group @mention rules, and desktop mirroring.

channels.description: Connect Buddy to Feishu / Lark, DingTalk, and future external apps. Receive messages, images, and files in real time and send Markdown or workspace artifacts back.
channels.extensibilityNote: Plugin-based channel architecture: Feishu WebSocket and DingTalk Stream are built in today, with Slack Socket, Telegram, and custom Webhooks ready to plug into the same surface.
channels.testSuccess: Connection healthy: identified bot "{{bot}}" in {{ms}} ms.

feishu.title: Feishu / Lark bot (WebSocket)
feishu.subtitle: No public domain, reverse proxy, or tunnel needed. Connects outbound via official Feishu WebSocket long connection.
feishu.guideHint: Expand for scopes & event subscription steps
feishu.step1: Create a custom app in Feishu Open Platform and enable the Bot capability.
feishu.step2: Open Permissions & Scopes, click Batch Import, and paste the recommended scopes JSON below.
feishu.step3: Under Events & Callbacks -> Event Configuration, choose "Receive events via persistent WebSocket connection" and subscribe to im.message.receive_v1.
feishu.step4: Publish a new app version, paste App ID & App Secret below, test the connection, and toggle on.
feishu.domainHint: Choose Feishu (feishu.cn) for China mainland or Lark (larksuite.com) for global.
feishu.secretSavedHint: App Secret is encrypted in your OS keychain and never echoed back. Leave blank to keep unchanged.

dingtalk.title: DingTalk Bot (Stream Mode)
dingtalk.subtitle: No public domain or reverse proxy required. Bidirectional Markdown, image, and workspace file delivery over DingTalk Stream + OpenAPI.
dingtalk.guideHint: Expand for Stream mode & permission steps
dingtalk.step1: Create an Enterprise Internal App in DingTalk Developer Portal and enable the Robot capability.
dingtalk.step2: In the Robot settings, set Message Receiving Mode to "Stream Mode".
dingtalk.step3: Enable permissions for sending enterprise robot messages and downloading robot message files.
dingtalk.step4: Publish a version of the app, paste Client ID (AppKey) & Client Secret below, test the connection, and toggle on.
dingtalk.secretSavedHint: Client Secret is encrypted in your OS keychain and never echoed back. Leave blank to keep unchanged.
dingtalk.robotCodeHint: Usually identical to Client ID for internal apps; leave blank to default to Client ID.
dingtalk.robotCodePlaceholder: Leave blank to reuse Client ID
dingtalk.mirrorHint: Keep inbound DingTalk requests and Buddy's external replies visible in your desktop Assistant stream.
dingtalk.targetsEmpty: No active DingTalk chats recorded yet. Send a message to your bot in DingTalk to populate this list.

access.title: Access control & pairing
access.desc: Guard against unknown senders or noisy group chats before inbound events reach Buddy.
access.dmPolicyHint: Default "Pairing": unknown senders get a friendly wait reply and queue an approval card above.
access.dmListHint: Users approved via pairing are added here automatically.
access.groupPolicyHint: Default "@Buddy only" ignores ambient group chatter.
access.groupListHint: When set to "Allowlist groups", only messages in these chats reach Buddy.

behavior.title: Session behavior
behavior.desc: Control how external channel chats interact with your desktop workspace.
behavior.mirrorHint: Keep inbound Feishu requests and Buddy's external replies visible in your desktop Assistant stream.
behavior.thinkingHint: Adds a 🤔 reaction on inbound Feishu messages while Buddy works, then clears it after replying.

targets.title: Known external chat targets
targets.desc: Buddy can inspect and push proactive updates or scheduled reports to these recent chats.
targets.empty: No active external chats recorded yet. Send a message to your bot in Feishu to populate this list.

memory.title: What it remembers
memory.desc: Local Markdown memory workbench: user profile, hard rules, pitfall playbook, and topic notes.

toolsTab.title: Callable tools
toolsTab.description: {{count}} tools, grouped by the extension that provides them; the number on the right is how many executors can call it.

mcp.title: MCP servers
mcp.description: Model Context Protocol: bring in outside tools (databases, internal APIs, someone else's service) so they show up in an agent's tool list like the built-in ones.
mcp.emptyHint: This tab is a placeholder: OPC has no MCP client yet, so there is nothing real to list. Once it exists, each server appears here the way extensions do — with its connection state and the tools it exposes.
mcp.needClient: A stdio / SSE client that starts the process or connects to the endpoint, with reconnect and exit handling
mcp.needTools: A translation from MCP tools to pi-durable tools, prefixed so names cannot collide with built-ins
mcp.needPolicy: The existing trust gate and per-executor switches — an MCP server can read local data too

external.title: Pi extensions on this machine
external.description: Discovered from ~/.pi/agent/extensions and .pi/extensions, the same places Pi itself auto-loads. Scanning only reads files; turning one on imports its code into the main process.
external.emptyHint: Drop a .ts file or a folder with index.ts into one of the directories above, then refresh. Packages installed with `pi install` are read from Pi's own npm folder automatically.
external.lazyHint: Turn it on to import it and see which tools it registers.
external.groupDescription: A Pi extension on this machine. Its switch lives in "Pi extensions on this machine" above; turning it off removes it from every agent.
external.trustBody: This extension is ordinary JavaScript, not a sandboxed plugin. Once enabled it runs inside the main process with the same rights as OPC itself.

trustRisk.code: Runs any code, including on startup
trustRisk.data: Can read the workspace database, workspaces, API keys and session history
trustRisk.network: Can call the network on its own

skills.title: Local skills
skills.description: Document tools and reusable domain workflows for executors, active automatically when turned on.
skills.emptyLocalHint: Place a folder containing SKILL.md into any directory below, then refresh.
skills.summary: {{enabled}} of {{total}} enabled — about {{tokens}} extra prompt tokens per request
skills.emptyHint: Drop a folder with a SKILL.md into one of the locations above, then refresh. Scripts a skill ships with still run through the bash tool and remain subject to sandbox policy.

skillPacks.title: Built-in office skills

skillPacks.sandboxUnavailable: Sandbox backend unavailable ({{detail}}): executors cannot run bash skill scripts on this platform.

capabilities.extensionsHint: Grouped by built-in module. Click any card to inspect its tools. External MCP tools are managed on the MCP page.
capabilities.extensionsHintSecondary: Conditional capabilities install per runtime: without a configured image/voice model, or with no other executor, the related tools do not appear.
capabilities.agentHint: Expand an executor to see what is installed in its own registry. Skill tags are for display only and never enter the prompt.

tools.read: Read a file in the workspace.
tools.write: Create or overwrite a workspace file.
tools.edit: Apply exact text edits to a workspace file.
tools.bash: Run a shell command inside the sandboxed workspace.
tools.generate_image: Generate an image from a prompt into the workspace.
tools.generate_video: Generate a video clip from a prompt and optional reference images into the workspace.
tools.transcribe_audio: Turn a workspace audio file into text.
tools.text_to_speech: Synthesize text into an audio file.
tools.remember: Save one durable lesson for future tasks.
tools.decompose_task: Split a task into subtasks for other executors.
tools.decide: Judge a piece of evidence and return a label, a score or a probability.

capabilities.loadError: Could not read the capability catalogue: {{message}}

work.title: Workflow tasks
work.description: Turns a task card into a durable, resumable, reviewable task that survives a crash.

coding.title: Files & commands
coding.description: Read, write, and edit workspace files, and run shell commands — the base of every deliverable.

sandbox.title: Sandbox policy
sandbox.description: The single gate for every tool call: constrains paths and wraps commands in the OS sandbox.

image.title: Image generation
image.description: Calls the configured image model and writes the resulting picture into the workspace.

video.title: Video generation
video.description: Calls the configured video model (text-to-video / image-to-video) and saves the clip into the workspace.

speech.title: Speech
speech.description: Transcription and synthesis; only the enabled half is installed.

ocr.title: Text recognition
ocr.description: Reads text out of images for models without vision.

memory.title: Long-term memory
memory.description: Saves a lesson to personal memory for the agent's future self.

comm.title: Colleague messaging
comm.description: Message a colleague, look up the latest conversation, acknowledge; it spends their wake quota.

decompose.title: Task decomposition
decompose.description: Splits a large task into subtasks for other executors; not installed when the workspace has only one.

decision.title: Structured decisions
decision.description: Calls the configured decision model (Jev / System One) to turn evidence into labels, scores or probabilities; installed only when a model is usable.

skills.title: Local skills
skills.description: Lists the skills in ~/.agents/skills in the system prompt and gives the agent a read_skill tool to load one in full on demand.

browser.title: Browser control
browser.description: Opens pages, interacts with elements, and reads web content inside a managed browser session.

desktop.title: Desktop control
desktop.description: Performs permission-gated desktop window, screen, and OS-level interactions.

assistantTools.title: Common web & utility tools
assistantTools.description: Provides time, weather, web lookup, and everyday calculation helpers.

recall.title: History recall
recall.description: Searches past work lines and conversation logs on demand to restore task context.

trace.title: Execution trace
trace.description: Passively records tool calls made by executors for auditing and debugging.

escalate.title: Escalation
escalate.description: Escalates blockers or decisions up to the coordinator when an executor needs intervention.

handback.title: Task handback
handback.description: Hands control back to the coordinator when work falls outside the executor's boundary.

investigate.title: Status investigation
investigate.description: Inspects subtask progress, failure logs, and environment state for diagnostics.

welcome.subtitle: Instant chat, background execution, long-term memory, browser & MCP tools, and your desktop companion Buddy — all ready in one workspace.
welcome.pressSuffix: to start · everything stays editable in Settings
welcome.capChatDesc: Fast replies in chat, steady background execution for complex goals.
welcome.capMemoryDesc: Remembers your name, tone, rules and ongoing context over time.
welcome.capToolsDesc: Web search, browser, desktop control, skills and scheduled runs.
welcome.capLocalDesc: Data and API keys stay encrypted locally; external actions ask first.

profile.title: What should I call you, and how should I reply?

previewSample.professional: Hello {{name}}. Share the objective and constraints, and I will execute and report back systematically.
